# Introduction

## Svamp project information - cross sectional analysis vaginal swabs

Vaginal swabs part of the svamp project were analyzed with shotgun sequencing. Taxonomic annotation was performed using the MetaPhlAn database 4.0.6. Quality control and filtering was performed previously and scripts can be found on the server: Groups/Kristina Broliden/Svamp_raw_data/Analysis/Metagenomics/... The aim is to investigate the difference in taxonomic profiles between patient groups: RVVCpos, RVVCneg, AS and Control. Cross sectional groups were defined by culture and self-reported symptom score:

-   RVVCpos: positive culture for C. albicans, symptom score \>= 1, \> 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as RVVCcul.pos

-   RVVCneg: negative culture, \> 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as RVVCcul.neg

-   AS: positive culture, symptom score = 0, =\< 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as CTRLcul.pos

-   Control: negative culture, =\< 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as CTRLcul.neg

In addition, the clinical score was used as a factor from score 0 to 5, to compare microbiome composition across an increasing score of inflammation. This score was determined by a experienced gynecologist and consisted of five categories marked present (1) or absent (0).

-   Fissures

-   Hyphae

-   Dryness

-   Discharge

-   Redness

Besides this, bulk transcriptomic data on the same vaginal swabs was used as inspiration for grouping of RVVCpos samples. In this previously published data (<https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/aji.70040>) two distinct clusters of RVVCpos samples were observed in the UMAP, one seperate cluster with high overall clinical scores and one cluster that mixes in with all the other diverse cross sectional samples and generally had a lower clinical score. These two clusters were used to subdivide the RVVCpos group into RVVCpos_seperate and RVVCpos_diverse for additional microbiome analysis.

All created output can be found on the server following: \~/Groups/Kristina Broliden/HIV group/Margaux/R work metagenomics + imaging/Luminal_cross_sectional

## Overview data analysis

For each set-up of analysis a similar data analysis approach was used:

-   Sample selection and renormalization

-   Alpha diversity (Shannon, Inverse Simpson and Species number)

-   Beta diversity using Bray-Curtis distance, creating a PCoA plot

-   Anosim

-   Permanova

-   Differential abundance analysis using Aldex2, visualized by a volcano plot

-   Barplots of relative abundance top 15 most abundant species

-   Community state type classification using Valencia

-   Heatmap of relative abundance

-   Clinical score presence

-   Network between species (correlation)

-   Major bacteria presence

## Import data

Relative abundance data in percentage was the output from the taxonomic annotation. The afterkraken2 count indicating the host removed counts by mapping against the human genome version GRCh38 using Kraken2 v2.0.8-beta is also available. Metadata including clinical and medical history data is available for all patients. Identification of samples is performed using the barcodes of vaginal swab samples and matching these to their svamp_IDs.

```{r}
#| label: import_data
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

##############
#IMPORT DATA #
##############

#relative abundance data (in percentage)
mp4_samplerows_no_run_repeat <- read_csv("~/R_work/Clinical_trial_CHG_FLZ/250321_mpa4_no_run_repeat.csv")

#count data
count_data <- read_csv("~/R_work/Clinical_trial_CHG_FLZ/250514_prepro_no_run_repeat.csv")

#clinicaldata
clinical_data <- read_xlsx("~/Desktop/Metadata_svamp_FINAL.xlsx")

#sample selection data
sample_identification <- read_xlsx("~/Desktop/svamp_ID_list.xlsx")
```

In the relative abundance file after quality control and filtering, 55 species and 151 patient samples are included. The count data file is present for these same patients.

## Additional filtering

```{r}
#| label: filtering
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

############
# SPIKE IN #
############

#Alicyclobacillus acidiphilus was a spike in the negative control samples

mp4_samplerows_no_run_repeat <- mp4_samplerows_no_run_repeat %>%
dplyr::select(-c("s__Alicyclobacillus_acidiphilus"))

```

Alicyclobacillus acidiphilus was found used in both the sequencing and extraction negative controls as a spike in + was found in some patient samples. It is therefore removed from the relative abundance data set.

## Sample selection

Specific samples of interest in the RVVC cross sectional groups are selected based on the barcodes applied to the vaginal swabs.

```{r}
#| label: sample-selection
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true
#| results: 'hide'

####################
# SAMPLE SELECTION #
####################

mp4_samplerows_no_run_repeat <- mp4_samplerows_no_run_repeat %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample_rowname")

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional <- mp4_samplerows_no_run_repeat %>%
  mutate(barcode_shotgun_swab = str_extract(rownames(mp4_samplerows_no_run_repeat), "(?<=__)[A-Za-z0-9]+(?=__)"))

#match with the ones in the sample identification file 
sample_identification_cross <- sample_identification %>%
    filter(group_cross %in% c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"))

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional %>%
  filter(barcode_shotgun_swab %in% sample_identification_cross$barcode_shotgun_swab)

#see if all are matching 
setdiff(sample_identification_cross$barcode_shotgun_swab, mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered$barcode_shotgun_swab) 
    #2 samples are not in the sample_rowname file but that makes sense because these are removed during filtering 

#merge the two files (relative abundance and sample identification, make sure to also merge the sample_rowname column since this is needed later)
mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_rowname")
  
merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional <- left_join(sample_identification_cross, mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered, by = "barcode_shotgun_swab")


#add the sample_rowname column to the sample identification file because will be needed later 
sample_identification_cross <- sample_identification_cross %>%
  left_join(merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>% dplyr::select(sample_rowname, barcode_shotgun_swab), by = "barcode_shotgun_swab")


#also do sample selection for the count df 
count_data_cross_sectional <- count_data %>%
  filter(sample_rowname %in% merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional$sample_rowname)
```

When matching the sample identification barcode column to the barcodes in the relative abundance data, two more samples (S10 and S15) are present in the sample identification file because these were filtered out from the relative abundance file. S10 had a too low read count and S15 did not reach 60% relative abundance with the applied taxa. These were now removed from the relative abundance file. Overall, after sample selection 78 samples remained.

## Renormalize

The sum in relative abundance per sample is renormalized to 100 across all included taxa.

```{r}
#| label: renormalize
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

###############
# RENORMALIZE #
###############

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(SUM = sum(c_across(2:55), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(across(2:55, ~ (. / SUM) * 100)) %>%
  mutate(SUM_CHECK = sum(c_across(2:55), na.rm = TRUE)) 
 

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized %>% 
  dplyr::select(-SUM, -SUM_CHECK)

write_csv(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/data files/251218_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_samplerows_filtered_renormalized.csv")
```

# Cross sectional groups

The microbial composition is characterized across the four previously described cross-sectional groups:

-   RVVCpos: positive culture for C. albicans, symptom score \>= 1, \> 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as RVVCcul.pos

-   RVVCneg: negative culture, \> 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as RVVCcul.neg

-   AS: positive culture, symptom score = 0, =\< 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as CTRLcul.pos

-   Control: negative culture, =\< 2 episodes RVVC per year, now known as CTRLcul.neg

## Alpha diversity

Alpha diversity including Shannon diversity, Inverse Simpson diversity and the species number are calculated for all samples. Comparisons are made between cross sectional groups, comparing the means. If there would be significant differences this would be highlighted in the figures by \*.

```{r}
#| label: alpha-diversity
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

###################
# ALPHA DIVERSITY #
###################

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample_rowname")

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized <- as.data.frame(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized)

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric))

shann_cross_df <- vegan::diversity(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized,index = c("shannon") )
simp_cross_df <- vegan::diversity(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized,index  = c("simpson") )
invsimp_cross_df <- vegan::diversity(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized,index  = c("invsimpson") )
spec_cross_df <-as.numeric(vegan::specnumber(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized))
divers_cross <- as.matrix(rbind(shann_cross_df,simp_cross_df,invsimp_cross_df,spec_cross_df) )
divers_cross[is.infinite(divers_cross)] <- 0
rownames(divers_cross) <- c("Shannon","simpson","Inv Simpson","SpecNo")

divers_t_cross <-as.data.frame(t(divers_cross))%>%
  mutate(sample_ID=colnames(divers_cross))

divers_t_cross <- divers_t_cross %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_rowname")

metadata_divers_cross <- sample_identification_cross %>%
  left_join(divers_t_cross, by = "sample_rowname")

metadata_divers_cross <- metadata_divers_cross %>%
  mutate(group_cross = factor(group_cross, 
                                  levels = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control")))


shann2_cross <- ggplot(metadata_divers_cross, aes (x=group_cross,y=Shannon,group=group_cross)) +
  geom_violin() +
  #geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(height = .2, width = .05)) +
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.2, size = 3) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", width = 0.8,colour = "#B2007F", linewidth = 1.5)+theme_classic()+ggtitle("Shannon") +
  #stat_compare_means(label="p.signif",comparisons = list(c("RVVCpos","RVVCneg"),c("RVVCpos","AS"),c("RVVCpos","Control"),c("RVVCneg","AS"),c("RVVCneg","Control"),c("AS","Control")), hide.ns = FALSE, size = 10, bracket.size = 2 ) +
  labs(y = "Shannon", title = NULL) +
  scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
         axis.title.y = element_text(size = 25, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, angle = 90, margin = margin(r = 20)), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, angle = 90, vjust = 0.5), 
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20))

plot(shann2_cross)  

shann2_cross <- ggplot(metadata_divers_cross, aes (x=group_cross,y=Shannon,group=group_cross)) +
  geom_violin() +
  #geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(height = .2, width = .05)) +
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.2, size = 3) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", width = 0.8,colour = "#B2007F", linewidth = 1.5)+theme_classic()+ggtitle("Shannon") +
   stat_compare_means(method = "kruskal.test", label.y = 4.5) +
  labs(y = "Shannon", title = NULL) +
  theme_classic() + 
  scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
         axis.title.y = element_text(size = 25, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, angle = 90, margin = margin(r = 20)), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, angle = 90, vjust = 0.5), 
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20))  




plot(shann2_cross)


simp2_cross <- ggplot(metadata_divers_cross, aes(x = group_cross, y = `Inv Simpson`, group = group_cross)) +
  geom_violin() +
  #geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(height = .2, width = .2)) +
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.2, size = 3) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", width = 0.8, colour = "#B2007F", linewidth = 1.5) +
  ggtitle("Inverse Simpson") +
  #stat_compare_means(
    #label = "p.signif", 
    #comparisons = list(c("RVVCpos","RVVCneg"),c("RVVCpos","AS"),c("RVVCpos","Control"),c("RVVCneg","AS"),c("RVVCneg","Control"),c("AS","Control")), size = 10, bracket.size = 2 
  #) +
  labs(y = "Inverse Simpson", title = NULL) +
  scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 25, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, angle = 90, margin = margin(r = 20)), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, angle = 90, vjust = 0.5), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20)
  )
  
plot(simp2_cross)


spec2_cross <- ggplot(metadata_divers_cross, aes (x=group_cross,y=SpecNo,group=group_cross)) +
  geom_violin() +
  #geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(height = .2, width = .2)) +
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.2, size = 3) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", width = 0.8,colour = "#B2007F", linewidth = 1.5)+theme_classic()+ggtitle("Species Number") +
  #stat_compare_means(label="p.signif",comparisons = list(c("RVVCpos","RVVCneg"),c("RVVCpos","AS"),c("RVVCpos","Control"),c("RVVCneg","AS"),c("RVVCneg","Control"),c("AS","Control")), size = 10, bracket.size = 2 ) +
  labs(y = "Species number", title = NULL) +
 scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
         axis.title.y = element_text(size = 25, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, angle = 90, margin = margin(r = 20)), 
        axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, angle = 90, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5), 
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20))

plot(spec2_cross)

ggsave("~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/alpha/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_shann_2by2.png", plot = shann2_cross, width = 12, height = 10)
ggsave("~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/alpha/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_simp_2by2.png", plot = simp2_cross, width = 12, height = 10)
ggsave("~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/alpha/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_spec_2by2.png", plot = spec2_cross, width = 12, height = 10)
```

## Beta diversity

A dimensionality reduction is performed on Bray-Curtis distances (non-metric multidimensionality scaling) to display the abundance data in a 2D manner. This is first visualized by cross sectional group and then by contributing bacterial species. Bray-Curtis is an applicable choice as it accounts for abundance of taxa no just absence or presence, so it helps to differentiate between crispatus dominant low diversity communities and high diversity polymicrobial communities.

```{r}
#| label: beta-diversity
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

##################
# BETA DIVERSITY #
##################

ordination_dysp_cross <-vegan::metaMDS(as.data.frame(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized[,1:54]), distance="bray", plot=FALSE,autotransform = FALSE)

points_dysp_cross <-data.frame(ordination_dysp_cross$points[,1:2])

points_dysp_cross <- points_dysp_cross %>% 
  mutate(sample_rowname = rownames(points_dysp_cross))

meta_dysp_cross <- left_join(points_dysp_cross, sample_identification_cross)

meta_dysp_cross$group_cross <- factor(meta_dysp_cross$group_cross, 
                                                        levels = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"))

my_colors <- c(
  "RVVCpos" = "#F06F6F",  
  "RVVCneg" = "#8BBF45",  
  "AS"      = "#4ABAC0",  
  "Control" = "#9B5DE5"   
)


pcoa_cross <-ggplot(data=meta_dysp_cross, aes(x=MDS1, y=MDS2,)) +
  xlim(-1.2,1.2) +
  ylim(-1.2,1.7) +
  geom_point(size=8, aes(color=group_cross), alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = group_cross, color = group_cross), 
               type = "t",        
               level = 0.95,      
               linetype = 1,      
               linewidth = 1) +
  #geom_jitter(aes(color = group_assigned), size = 8, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.05, height = 0.05) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggtitle("MDS Bray") +
  scale_colour_manual(
  values = my_colors,
  breaks = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = number_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = number_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
    legend.title = element_text(size = 25, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 25, face = "bold"), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20), 
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20), 
    legend.position = "right"
  )

plot(pcoa_cross)

ggsave(plot = pcoa_cross, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/beta/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_beta_diversity_combined.png", width = 16, height = 12, dpi = 300)


#Overlay with major species 

meta_dysp2_cross <- left_join(points_dysp_cross, merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional, by = c("sample_rowname"))

meta_dysp2_cross$group_cross <- factor(meta_dysp2_cross$group_cross, 
                                                        levels = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"))
```

No immediate clustering is visible based on cross sectional groups but when the PCoA is overlayed with bacterial presence a pattern appears. What we can see is that the RVVCpos group seems to cluster on the left of MDS1 while Control seems more spread along MDS1. Both RVVCneg and AS cluster in the middle of MDS1 and 2, also somewhat in the middle of the RVVCpos and Control group, but this could also be due to the smaller sample size in these two groups. RVVCneg and AS are more tightly clustered (also reflected in smallest amount of species number) but this could also be due to sample size.

When overlaying the PCoA with the top three major bacteria (*L. crispatus. L. iners and G. vaginalis*), these form the hubs for the main cluster points of the data. This does also show that the RVVCpos samples cluster more towards *G. vaginalis* and *L. iners* but away from *L. crispatus*. While RVVCneg and AS do not cluster towards *G. vaginalis* and only towards *L. iners* and *L. crispatus*. The Control groups seems to be spread over all the hubs. *C. albicans* seems to be mainly co-localized with *L.iners* hub.

## Anosim

Anosim tests to see if differences between groups are larger than the differences within groups based on a distance matrix (Bray-Curtis).

```{r}
#| label: anosim
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

##########
# ANOSIM #
##########

#remove SUM column 
merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional <- merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>%
    dplyr::select(-SUM)

#remove the NA rows (the two filtered out samples S10 and S15)
merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional <- merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>%
  dplyr::filter(!svamp_ID %in% c("S10", "S15"))

dist_matrix_cross <- vegdist(merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional[, 17:70], method = "bray", na.rm = TRUE)

#run anosim on the distance matrix
anosim(dist_matrix_cross, group = merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional$group_cross, permutations = 999)

#0.448 not significant so the permutation ANOVA can be run 
```

The result of the anosim is a significance of 0.463 which is not significant. This means that between group differences do not differ from within group differences more than expected to happen by chance. So the microbial community overlaps substantially between the different research groups. So the slight visual differences seen in the PCoA plots have substantial overlap and are not statistically significant from each other.

## PERMANOVA

Even though it seems there are no differences in microbial structure between group, we follow this up by a PERMANOVA analysis. This tests if microbial compositions differ significantly between groups.

### Overall

```{r}
#| label: permanova
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

#############
# PERMANOVA #
#############

vegan::adonis2(merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional[,17:70]~group_cross, data = merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional, na.action = na.omit, permutations = 999,method="bray") #0.068


#Do any of the factors have an effect on the significance (those that are sig in Table 1)

#vegan::adonis2(data_AS_Control[,2:49]~chlamydia+group_assigned, data = data_AS_Control, na.action = na.omit, permutations = 999,method="bray", by = "margin") #0.734 

```

The model explains about 7% of the variation seen in the data (so explained by the grouping), this is a very low number and is also not significant since the p-value is 0.098. Overall no statistically clear clusters in data based on cross sectional grouping.

### AS - RVVCpos subsampling

```{r}
#| label: permanova - AS-RVVCpos
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

data_AS_RVVCpos_cross <- merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>%
  filter(group_cross %in% c("AS", "RVVCpos"))

vegan::adonis2(data_AS_RVVCpos_cross[,17:70]~group_cross, data = data_AS_RVVCpos_cross, na.action = na.omit, permutations = 999,method="bray") #0.05 SIGNIFICANT!

#Subsample to make sure if it really is sig. (because RVVCpos is larger group than AS) then take a random 7 sample subsample of the RVVCpos 10 times, and run against the AS group, only if sig 5 times it really is sig.

library(scutr)

#RVVCpos VS AS 

set.seed(1234)
 
m <- 0
SB_undersampled_list <- list()
result1<-data.frame()
Adonis_results<-data.frame()
input<-merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional%>%filter(!is.na(group_cross))
table(input$group_cross)
for (i in 1:10) {
  m <- m + 1
 
  SB_undersample_1 <- resample_random(input, "RVVCpos","group_cross", 7)
 
  SB_subsampled <- filter(input, group_cross %in% c("AS"))
  SB_subsampled <- rbind(SB_undersample_1,SB_subsampled)
  species_input_sampled_SB <- SB_subsampled[,17:70]
  form2 <- as.formula(paste("species_input_sampled_SB","group_cross",sep="~"))
  SB_undersampled_list[[m]] <- vegan::adonis2(form2, data = SB_subsampled[,c(17:70,7)], na.action = na.omit, method="euclidian",permutations = 99)
  print(m)
  print(SB_undersampled_list[[m]][1,5])
  result1[m,1]<-SB_undersampled_list[[m]][1,3]
  result1[m,2]<-SB_undersampled_list[[m]][1,5]
}
temp<-result1%>%
  arrange(V2,desc(V1)) #V2 is the p value
print(temp)
Adonis_results[1,c(1,2,3)]<-c("group_cross",temp[1,1],temp[1,2])
```

Almost 9% of variation in taxa explained by grouping between AS and RVVCpos, significant difference. However the AS group has a much smaller sample size. So the account for this the RVVCpos group was subsampled to match the size of the AS group 10 times randomly and then analysis was run again. For only 3 comparisons the p-value indicated significance. This means there is larger variability in the RVVCpos group and thus when a subsample is taken it can differ so much in composition that differences in results will occur (some subsamples will match AS more than others). So there really is no robust difference between AS and RVVCpos.

Reduced model (candida and group evaluated jointly): The overall model is statistically significant, meaning that together\
s\_\_Candida_albicans + group_cross explain more variation than expected by chance. The model significantly explains 12% of the variance in the data.

Individual predictors: Candida albicans explains \~4.4% of Bray–Curtis variation

This effect is independent of group_cross, No evidence that groups differ in centroid location after controlling for Candida

## Differential abundance analysis

Differential abundance analysis is performed with Aldex2. This is a method designed to identify features that are differently abundant between experimental conditions while accounting for the compositional nature of the sequencing data. Compositional data means that our data is relative, not absolute. We know the proportion of reads per feature (relative abundance) which means that if one feature increases in number the other needs to appear to decrease even in absolute numbers it doesn't (= compositional effect). Regular statistics can thus induce false positives or negatives since they assume absolute values. Aldex2 uses Dirichlet–Monte Carlo sampling and Centered Log-Ratio (CLR) transformation to model the nature of the data. Aldex2 requires a data frame with the samples as columns and the pathways as rows. The input data needs to be in the form of counts. Since we are working with relative abundance we can estimate the counts by multiplying the relative abundance per sample and pathway with the afterkraken2 read count (reads remaining after host removal). However, we need to use raw data and not previously normalized data since CLR normalization is done in the analysis itself. So first the raw read count pathway data needs to be transformed to relative abundance, then counts and then samples can be selected for analysis.

### Estimated counts

```{r}
#| label: estimated counts
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true
#| results: 'hide'

####################
# ESTIMATED COUNTS #
####################

#devtools::install_github("ggloor/ALDEx_bioc")

#if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    #install.packages("BiocManager")

#BiocManager::install("ALDEx2")

library(ALDEx2)

#relative abundance data filtered but not normalized - mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional

#counts data 
kraken_counts <- count_data %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "sample_rowname")

kraken_counts <- kraken_counts %>%
  mutate(barcode_shotgun_swab = str_extract(rownames(kraken_counts), "(?<=__)[A-Za-z0-9]+(?=__)"))

kraken_counts <- kraken_counts %>%
  left_join(sample_identification %>% dplyr::select(svamp_ID, barcode_shotgun_swab), by = "barcode_shotgun_swab")

#add the afterkraken column to the pathway abundance df

setdiff(kraken_counts$barcode_shotgun_swab, mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional$barcode_shotgun_swab)

estimated_counts <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional %>% 
left_join(kraken_counts %>% dplyr::select(svamp_ID, after_kraken2_host_removal, barcode_shotgun_swab), by ="barcode_shotgun_swab")

estimated_counts <- estimated_counts %>%
    dplyr::select(-SUM)

#the relative abundace should not be in percentage so it gets divided by 100 and then multiplied by the kraken reads
estimated_counts <- estimated_counts %>%
  mutate_at(vars(1:54), ~ after_kraken2_host_removal * 0.01 * .)
  
#counts as integers 
estimated_counts <- estimated_counts %>%
   mutate_at(c(1:54), as.integer)

write_csv(estimated_counts, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/data files/251218_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_estimated_counts.csv")
```

### AS VS RVVCpos

```{r}
#| label: aldex2 - ASRVVCpos
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true
#| results: 'hide'

#aldex metadata 
aldexmeta <- sample_identification %>%
  filter(group_cross %in% c("AS", "RVVCpos"))

#aldex data 
aldexdata <- estimated_counts

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>% 
  filter(svamp_ID %in% aldexmeta$svamp_ID) %>%
  mutate(svamp_ID = factor(svamp_ID, levels = aldexmeta$svamp_ID)) %>%
  arrange(svamp_ID)

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>% 
  tibble::column_to_rownames(var = "svamp_ID")

aldexdata <- t(aldexdata)

aldexdata <- as.data.frame(aldexdata)

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>% mutate_all(as.numeric)

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>%
  filter(!if_all(everything(), ~ . == 0))

aldexdata <- aldexdata[rownames(aldexdata) != "after_kraken2_host_removal", ]

#check if they match names
setdiff(colnames(aldexdata), aldexmeta$svamp_ID) #no differences

setdiff(aldexmeta$svamp_ID, colnames(aldexdata)) #S15

aldexmeta <- aldexmeta %>%
  filter(svamp_ID != "S15")

all.equal(names(aldexdata),c(aldexmeta$svamp_ID)) #TRUE


#Get the indices of the names in the same order
order_indices <- match(aldexmeta$svamp_ID, names(aldexdata))

#Reorder the columns to match the order 
aldexdata <- aldexdata[, order_indices]

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>%
mutate_at(c(1:37), as.integer)

#set the conditions to compare 
conds <-factor(aldexmeta$group_cross, levels=c("AS", "RVVCpos")) 

#vector needs to be character 
conds <- as.character(conds)

#aldex
x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross <- ALDEx2::aldex(aldexdata, conds, mc.samples=128, test="t", effect=TRUE,
     include.sample.summary=FALSE, denom="all", verbose=FALSE)

x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross <- x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "species")

write_csv(x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/differential abundance/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_dif_abundance_RVVCpos_AS.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: aldex2 - RVVCnegControl

#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true
#| results: 'hide'

#aldex metadata 
aldexmeta <- sample_identification %>%
  filter(group_cross %in% c("RVVCneg", "Control"))

#aldex data 
aldexdata <- estimated_counts

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>% 
  filter(svamp_ID %in% aldexmeta$svamp_ID) %>%
  mutate(svamp_ID = factor(svamp_ID, levels = aldexmeta$svamp_ID)) %>%
  arrange(svamp_ID)

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>% 
  tibble::column_to_rownames(var = "svamp_ID")

aldexdata <- t(aldexdata)

aldexdata <- as.data.frame(aldexdata)

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>% mutate_all(as.numeric)

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>%
  filter(!if_all(everything(), ~ . == 0))

aldexdata <- aldexdata[rownames(aldexdata) != "after_kraken2_host_removal", ]

#check if they match names
setdiff(colnames(aldexdata), aldexmeta$svamp_ID) #no differences

setdiff(aldexmeta$svamp_ID, colnames(aldexdata)) #S10

aldexmeta <- aldexmeta %>%
  filter(svamp_ID != "S10")

all.equal(names(aldexdata),c(aldexmeta$svamp_ID)) #TRUE


#Get the indices of the names in the same order
order_indices <- match(aldexmeta$svamp_ID, names(aldexdata))

#Reorder the columns to match the order 
aldexdata <- aldexdata[, order_indices]

aldexdata <- aldexdata %>%
mutate_at(c(1:41), as.integer)

#set the conditions to compare 
conds <-factor(aldexmeta$group_cross, levels=c("RVVCneg", "Control")) 

#vector needs to be character 
conds <- as.character(conds)

#aldex
x_all_RVVCneg_Control_cross <- ALDEx2::aldex(aldexdata, conds, mc.samples=128, test="t", effect=TRUE,
     include.sample.summary=FALSE, denom="all", verbose=FALSE)

x_all_RVVCneg_Control_cross <- x_all_RVVCneg_Control_cross %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "species")

write_csv(x_all_RVVCneg_Control_cross, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/differential abundance/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_dif_abundance_RVVCneg_Control.csv")
```

### Differential abundance table significant differences (before FDR)

After performing all the differential abundance analyses, the taxa that show up significant (we.ep \< 0.05) before adjusting of the p-value are combined into one table. This comprises all the performed 1 by 1 comparisons of cross sectional groups.

```{r}
#| label: differential-abundance-significant-cross
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

#list of dfs from the differential abundance analyses
df_names <- ls(pattern = "^x_all.*_cross$")

#combine significant results from all differential abundance analyses
combined_significant_aldex2 <- df_names %>%
  lapply(function(nm) {
    df <- get(nm)                
    df %>%
      filter(we.ep < 0.05) %>%  
      mutate(source_df = nm)      
  }) %>%
  bind_rows()                      

combined_significant_aldex2 %>%
gt()

write_csv(combined_significant_aldex2, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/differential abundance/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_dif_abundance_significant_taxa.csv")
```

Before accounting for multiple comparison biggest change in *C. albicans* (discussed in next section). Next, lower *L. iners* is seen in RVVCpos - AS and AS - Control, with a decrease seen compared to AS. Effect size is modest though. *L. gasseri* has a higher abudance in RVVCpos compared to RVVCneg, complemented with the same change for *Dialister micraerophilus*. These don't seem to be primary drivers of RVVC group differences.

## Differential abundance table significant differences (after FDR)

```{r}
#| label: differential-abundance-significant-cross-afterFDR
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

#list of dfs from the differential abundance analyses
df_names <- ls(pattern = "^x_all.*_cross$")

#combine significant results from all differential abundance analyses
combined_significant_aldex2_afterFDR <- df_names %>%
  lapply(function(nm) {
    df <- get(nm)                
    df %>%
      filter(we.eBH < 0.05) %>%  
      mutate(source_df = nm)      
  }) %>%
  bind_rows()                      

combined_significant_aldex2_afterFDR %>%
gt()

write_csv(combined_significant_aldex2_afterFDR, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/differential abundance/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_dif_abundance_significant_taxa_afterFDR.csv")
```

After accounting for multiple comparison the only species that remains significant is *Candida albicans*. Between the groups RVVCpos - Control and RVVCpos - RVVCneg we see the difference. The difference between (CLR normalized) are very big and both have a strong effect size. This means that *C. albicans* is the main driver of group differences observed between these groups. But it is also noticeable that after FDR all other species lose their significance. Meaning that there are no robust group differences. This matches what was found in the Permanova analysis where no real group differences were found. So overall these results are indicating that the microbiome is relatively stable across RVVC groups and that it is candida overgrowth but not changes in the microbial composition in the vagina that are the signature of RVVC. Thus RVVC does not seem to be a bacterial dysbiosis event but rather a fungal overgrowth event that can occur in any bacterial composition environment (or similar bacterial communities). Additionally, the difference in abundance and the effect sizes are very similar when comparing RVVCpos-Control and RVVCpos-RVVCneg, meaning that RVVCneg and Control are extremely close in composition. This follows literature as it is thought that RVVC works in episodic infections and not chronic low grade infection/colonization.

## Volcano plot differential abundant species - after FDR

A way of visualizing the differential abundance data is through a volcano plot. On the y-axis the Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value (we.eBH) is displayed after -log10 normalization for visualization purposes. The x-axis contains the log2 of the fold change (ratio of mean abundance of two conditions). Significance is cut off at a p-value of 0.05 and log2 fold change of 1 (= taxa with at least a 2× change between groups).

### AS - RVVCpos

```{r}
#| label: volcano-plot-AS-RVVCpos
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

species_levels <- unique(x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross$species)
species_count <- length(species_levels)

color_palette_volcano <- setNames(colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"))(species_count), species_levels)

significant_species_difabu <- x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  filter(abs(diff.btw) > 1 & we.eBH < 0.05)

significant_species <- significant_species_difabu$species #There are no significant species

#define cutoffs
fc_cutoff <- 1
p_cutoff <- 0.05

#is the species significant or not 
x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross <- x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      diff.btw > fc_cutoff & we.eBH < p_cutoff ~ "Up",
      diff.btw < -fc_cutoff & we.eBH < p_cutoff ~ "Down",
      TRUE ~ "Non-significant")
  )

#colors
volcano_colors <- c(
  "Up" = "hotpink",          #pink
  "Down" = "#2166ac",        # blue
  "Non-significant" = "gray70"
)

#volcano plot with cutoffs (significance and fold change)
volcano_difa_cutoffs_ASRVVCpos <- ggplot(x_all_AS_RVVCpos_cross,
                       aes(x = diff.btw, y = -log10(we.eBH), color = significance)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = volcano_colors) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-fc_cutoff, fc_cutoff), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(p_cutoff), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "log2 Fold Change",
    y = "-log10 adjusted p-value",
    title = "Volcano Plot: AS vs RVVCpos"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

plot(volcano_difa_cutoffs_ASRVVCpos)

ggsave("~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/differential abundance/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_volcano_AS_RVVCpos.png", plot = volcano_difa_cutoffs_ASRVVCpos, bg = "white", width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)

```

No species are found to be significantly different in abundance between the AS and RVVCpos group when looking at the adjusted p-value.

### RVVCneg - RVVCpos

```{r}
#| label: volcano-plot-RVVCneg-RVVCpos
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE

species_levels <- unique(x_all_RVVCneg_RVVCpos_cross$species)
species_count <- length(species_levels)

color_palette_volcano <- setNames(colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"))(species_count), species_levels)

significant_species_difabu <- x_all_RVVCneg_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  filter(abs(diff.btw) > 1 & we.eBH < 0.05)

significant_species <- significant_species_difabu$species #There is one significant species -> c. albicans 

#define cutoffs
fc_cutoff <- 1
p_cutoff <- 0.05

#is the species significant or not 
x_all_RVVCneg_RVVCpos_cross <- x_all_RVVCneg_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      diff.btw > fc_cutoff & we.eBH < p_cutoff ~ "Up",
      diff.btw < -fc_cutoff & we.eBH < p_cutoff ~ "Down",
      TRUE ~ "Non-significant"
    ),
    highlight = ifelse(species == "C. albicans", "C. albicans", "Other")
  )

#colors
volcano_colors <- c(
  "Up" = "hotpink",          #pink
  "Down" = "#2166ac",        # blue
  "Non-significant" = "gray70"
)

#labels in figure 
sig_species <- x_all_RVVCneg_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  filter(significance != "Non-significant") %>%
  mutate(pretty_label = ifelse(species == "s__Candida_albicans",
                               "italic('C. albicans')",  # string, not expression()
                               species))

#volcano plot with cutoffs (significance and fold change)
volcano_difa_cutoffs <- ggplot(x_all_RVVCneg_RVVCpos_cross,
                       aes(x = diff.btw, y = -log10(we.eBH), color = significance)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = volcano_colors) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-fc_cutoff, fc_cutoff), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(p_cutoff), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = sig_species,
    aes(label = pretty_label),
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 5,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "log2 Fold Change",
    y = "-log10 adjusted p-value",
    title = "Volcano Plot: RVVCcul.pos vs RVVCcul.neg"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

plot(volcano_difa_cutoffs)

ggsave("~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/differential abundance/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_volcano_RVVCneg_RVVCpos.png", plot = volcano_difa_cutoffs, bg = "white", width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
#| label: volcano-plot-RVVCpos-Control-beforeFDR

fc_cutoff <- 1
p_cutoff <- 0.05

#is the species significant or not 
x_all_RVVCpos_Control_cross <- x_all_RVVCpos_Control_cross %>%
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      diff.btw > fc_cutoff & we.ep < p_cutoff ~ "Up",
      diff.btw < -fc_cutoff & we.ep < p_cutoff ~ "Down",
      TRUE ~ "Non-significant"
    ),
    highlight = ifelse(species == "C. albicans", "C. albicans", "Other")
  )

#colors

      "italic('",
      gsub("_", " ", sub("^s__", "", species)),
      "')"
    )
  )

                       aes(x = diff.btw, y = -log10(we.ep), color = significance)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = volcano_colors) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-fc_cutoff, fc_cutoff), linetype = "dashed") +

    data = sig_species,
    aes(label = pretty_label),
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 5,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "log2 Fold Change",
    y = "-log10 adjusted p-value",
    title = "Volcano Plot: RVVCpos vs Control"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

## Major bacteria

The most abundantly present species per sample are identified based on their relative abundance.

```{r}
#| label: major-bacteria
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

##################
# MAJOR BACTERIA #
##################

#calculate the majority bacteria
with_maj_bac_cross <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    row_max = max(c_across(1:54)), 
    maj_bac = names(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized)[which.max(c_across(1:54))]
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

with_maj_bac_cross <- as.data.frame(with_maj_bac_cross)
 
row.names(with_maj_bac_cross)<-row.names(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized)

#calculate the second majority bacteria by first subtracting the majority % and then replace 0 with NA, and find new max
secondlargest_cross<-with_maj_bac_cross%>%
  mutate_at(vars(1:54), funs(abs(.-row_max))) %>%
  mutate(across(1:54, ~na_if(., 0)))%>%
  rowwise() %>%
mutate(maj_bac2nd = names(.)[which.min(c_across(1:54))])%>%
  rowwise()%>%
  mutate(maj_bac2nd_percent =min(c_across(1:54),na.rm=T))%>%
  mutate(maj_bac2nd_percent=abs(maj_bac2nd_percent-row_max))
secondlargest_cross$sample_rowname <-row.names(with_maj_bac_cross)

#lacto sum
lacto_cross <-  as.data.frame(names(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized))%>%filter(grepl("Lactobacillus",`names(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized)`))
lacto_sum_genus_cross <-with_maj_bac_cross[,c((names(with_maj_bac_cross) %in% lacto_cross$`names(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized)`))]%>%
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(lacto_sum_genus_cross=sum(c_across(1:nrow(lacto_cross))))
lacto_sum_genus_cross$sample_rowname<-row.names(with_maj_bac_cross)

#make one dataframe with majority (first and second) bacteria and lacto-sum
major_bac_cross<-left_join(secondlargest_cross[,c("row_max","maj_bac","maj_bac2nd","maj_bac2nd_percent","sample_rowname")],lacto_sum_genus_cross[,c("lacto_sum_genus_cross","sample_rowname")])%>%
  mutate(twobiggest=sum(row_max,maj_bac2nd_percent))

#add in the svamp_ID and the group_cross 
major_bac_cross <- major_bac_cross %>% 
  left_join(metadata_divers_cross %>% dplyr::select("svamp_ID", "group_cross", "sample_rowname"), by = "sample_rowname")

major_bac_cross %>%
gt()

write_csv(major_bac_cross, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/major bacteria/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_majority_bacteria.csv")

```

Four species were found to be the most abundant in at least one patient sample: *L. crispatus, L. iners, L. jensenii* and *G. vaginalis.*

## Lactobacilli

Besides just the major bacteria it is also interesting to see if there is a difference in lactobacilli presence across cross sectional groups. Comparisons of the total abundance in lactobacilli in the violin plot is done with the Mann Whitney U test.

```{r}
#| label: lactobacilli
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

################
# LACTOBACILLI #
################

#major_bac_cross has the information on the amount of total lactobacilli present per sample 

#in the differential abundance analysis we are already seeing the group difference per lactobacilli species -> non-normal (non-parametric) so have to do Kruskal-Wallis test

kruskal.test(lacto_sum_genus_cross ~ group_cross, data = major_bac_cross)

#post hoc 

dunnTest(lacto_sum_genus_cross ~ group_cross, data = major_bac_cross, method = "bh")

#violin plot 

lacto_plot <- ggplot(major_bac_cross, aes(x = group_cross, y = lacto_sum_genus_cross, group = group_cross)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(x = "Group", y = expression(italic("Lactobacillus") ~ "abundance (%)")) +
  geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(height = 0.2, width = 0.2), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = "mean", 
    geom = "crossbar", 
    width = 0.5, 
    color = "#B2007F"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  stat_compare_means(label="p.signif",exact = FALSE, comparisons = list(c("RVVCpos","RVVCneg"),c("RVVCpos", "AS"), c("RVVCpos", "Control")), size = 7, bracket.size = 0.7, tip.length = 0.02)  + 
   theme(
       axis.title.x = element_blank(),
       axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16), 
       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 90),
       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16)
   ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
 
plot(lacto_plot)

ggsave(plot = lacto_plot, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/major bacteria/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_violinplot_lactobacilli.png",  width = 16, height = 14, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

lacto_plot <- ggplot(major_bac_cross, aes(x = group_cross, y = lacto_sum_genus_cross, group = group_cross)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(x = "Group", y = expression(italic("Lactobacillus") ~ "abundance (%)")) +
  geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(height = 0.2, width = 0.2), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = "mean", 
    geom = "crossbar", 
    width = 0.5, 
    color = "#B2007F"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  #stat_compare_means(label="p.signif",exact = FALSE, comparisons = list(c("RVVCpos","RVVCneg"),c("RVVCpos", "AS"), c("RVVCpos", "Control")), size = 7, bracket.size = 0.7, tip.length = 0.02)  + 
   theme(
       axis.title.x = element_blank(),
       axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16), 
       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 90),
       axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16)
   ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
 
plot(lacto_plot)

```

The Kruskal-Wallis test indicates there is a difference in total lactobacilli amount between RVVC groups. After a post-hoc test it is shown that the amount doesn't differ between AS, Control and RVVCneg groups. But all these groups compared to RVVCpos show less lactobacilli in total for the RVVCpos group. After FDR this is not significant anymore but it does give slight biological indications. This could mean that candida overgrowth supresses overall lactobacilli, or if a overall reduction in lactobacilli creates a niche for candida overgrowth. And this shows that in terms of total lactobacilli AS seems to be distinct from RVVCpos.

## Relative abundance

The relative abundance of the top15 most abundantly present species across all cross sectional samples is presented in barplots per group and patient. All other species abundance is grouped in a category called other. The order of patients in the barplots is based on their abundance of the four major bacteria.

```{r}
#| label: relative-abundance
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

######################
# RELATIVE ABUNDANCE #
######################

#colors
group.colors <- c("s__Lactobacillus_crispatus" = "#148F77",
                  "s__Lactobacillus_iners" = "#A3E4D7", 
"s__Lactobacillus_gasseri" ="#6D9F06", 
"s__Lactobacillus_jensenii" = "#4E7705", 
"s__Gardnerella_vaginalis"= "#CC79A7",#"#7D3560", 
"s__Fannyhessea_vaginae"="#EFB6D6",#"#E794C1", 
"s__Streptococcus_agalactiae"="#FFD5AF", 
"s__Limosilactobacillus_portuensis"="#F09163", 
"s__Staphylococcus_aureus"="#566be9",
"s__Prevotella_bivia"="#fecf44", 
"other"="#8B8B8B", 
"s__Dialister_micraerophilus"="#ffe2c9", 
"s__Ureaplasma_parvum"="#ff7f00", 
"s__Aerococcus_christensenii"="#A569BD", 
"s__Candida_albicans"="#8B0000", 
"s__Megasphaera_lornae" = "#C17754") 

#include the major bac column 
ra_samplerows_cross <- merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>%
  left_join(major_bac_cross %>% dplyr::select(svamp_ID, maj_bac), by = "svamp_ID")

#make the major bac a factor so that samples get ordered by that (L. crispatus, L. iners, G. vaginalis, L. jensenii)
ra_samplerows_cross <- ra_samplerows_cross %>%
  mutate(maj_bac = factor(maj_bac, 
                                  levels = c("s__Lactobacillus_crispatus", "s__Lactobacillus_iners", "s__Gardnerella_vaginalis", "s__Lactobacillus_jensenii")))

#take only the 15 most abundant taxa for the graph all the others can be combined into an other category
column_sums_cross <- colSums(ra_samplerows_cross[, 17:70])

#top 15 most abundant species
column_sums_cross <- sort(column_sums_cross, decreasing = TRUE)
column_sums_df_cross <- as.data.frame(column_sums_cross)
column_sums_df_cross$species <- rownames(column_sums_df_cross)
first_15_cross <- column_sums_df_cross[1:15, ]

#data in long format 
ra_samplerows_long_cross <- ra_samplerows_cross %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("s__"),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "Abundance"
  )

#rename all the taxa that are not in top 15 to other
accepted_species_cross <- c("s__Lactobacillus_crispatus", "s__Lactobacillus_iners", "s__Gardnerella_vaginalis", "s__Lactobacillus_jensenii", "s__Lactobacillus_gasseri", "s__Fannyhessea_vaginae", "s__Aerococcus_christensenii", "s__Megasphaera_lornae", "s__Limosilactobacillus_portuensis","s__Staphylococcus_aureus","s__Prevotella_bivia", "s__Streptococcus_agalactiae", "s__Candida_albicans", "s__Ureaplasma_parvum", "s__Dialister_micraerophilus")                        

ra_samplerows_long_other_cross <- ra_samplerows_long_cross %>%
  mutate(Species = ifelse(Species %in% accepted_species_cross, Species, "other"))

#subset the data to the different groups 
ra_RVVCpos_cross <- ra_samplerows_long_other_cross %>% 
  filter(group_cross %in% "RVVCpos")

ra_RVVCneg_cross <- ra_samplerows_long_other_cross %>% 
  filter(group_cross %in% "RVVCneg")

ra_AS_cross <- ra_samplerows_long_other_cross %>% 
  filter(group_cross %in% "AS")

ra_Control_cross <- ra_samplerows_long_other_cross %>% 
  filter(group_cross %in% "Control")

#make svamp_ID a factor and order based on maj bac 
ra_RVVCpos_cross$svamp_ID <- as.factor(ra_RVVCpos_cross$svamp_ID)

ra_RVVCpos_cross <- ra_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  mutate(maj_bac = factor(maj_bac, 
                                  levels = c("s__Lactobacillus_crispatus", "s__Lactobacillus_iners", "s__Gardnerella_vaginalis", "s__Lactobacillus_jensenii")))

ra_RVVCpos_cross$svamp_ID <- factor(ra_RVVCpos_cross$svamp_ID, 
                                      levels = unique(ra_RVVCpos_cross$svamp_ID[order(ra_RVVCpos_cross$maj_bac)]))

ra_RVVCpos_cross <- ra_RVVCpos_cross %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  mutate(TotalAbundance = sum(Abundance)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Species = reorder(Species, TotalAbundance))
```

## CST classification Valencia

VALENCIA is a nearest-centroid based algorithm for the classification of human vaginal microbial community into state types based on their taxonomic composition. Samples are individually assigned to community state types (CSTs) based on their similarity to a set of thirteen reference centroids. (<https://github.com/ravel-lab/VALENCIA>). Per cross sectional group a bar plot is made showcasing the CST per patient, this will later be combined with the relative abundance plot. Additionally, the CST subdivision of each patient is represented in a table. Here per cross sectional group the number of patients per sub type of CST is clearly represented. The last column of the table shows the p-values calculated by a chi-square test, to see if there is a difference in subCST distribution across cross sectional groups.

To obtain the CST types, the script obtained through github needs to be run in python (through the terminal). The input file needs to have samples as rows and species are columns. The first column is the ID, second is the total read count per sample and following are species read counts. Since we have relative abundance, the reads need to be estimated by multiplying the relative abundance (in a fraction of 0 - 1) with the read count after host removal.

```{r}
#| label: CST-Valencia-classification
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

################
# CST VALENCIA #
################

#merge the relative abundance with the after kraken2 column (select kraken column and add to filtered and renormalized relative abundance data)
count_kraken_cross <- count_data_cross_sectional %>% dplyr::select(-Sample, -duplication, -before_fastp, -after_fastp)

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized %>%
rownames_to_column(var = "sample_rowname")

reads_CST <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized %>%
  left_join(count_kraken_cross %>% dplyr::select("after_kraken2_host_removal", "sample_rowname"), by = "sample_rowname")

mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized <- mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized %>%
column_to_rownames("sample_rowname")

#the relative abundance data is in percentage now and needs to be adjusted to 0-1 range by multiplying by 0.01 and multiply each relative abundance measure with the total read count of that sample (the after kraken 2 column)
reads_CST <- reads_CST %>%
 mutate_at(vars(2:55), ~ after_kraken2_host_removal * 0.01 * .)

#adapt the names of the columns 1 and 2 to match with the required input (get barcodes from another df, first column named sampleID, second read_count)
reads_CST_python <- reads_CST %>%
left_join(merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>% dplyr::select("svamp_ID", "sample_rowname"), by = "sample_rowname")

reads_CST_python <- reads_CST_python %>%
dplyr::select(-sample_rowname)

reads_CST_python <- reads_CST_python %>%
rename(sampleID = svamp_ID)

reads_CST_python <- reads_CST_python %>%
rename(read_count = after_kraken2_host_removal)

reads_CST_python <- reads_CST_python %>%
relocate(sampleID, .before = 1)

reads_CST_python <- reads_CST_python %>%
relocate(read_count, .before = 2)

write_csv(reads_CST_python, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/Output/CST/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_estimated_counts_for_CST.csv")

#adjust the names of the species to columns to match with the names used in valencia
valencia_names <- read_csv("~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/data/250519_Metaphlan_to_Valencia_translation.csv")

name_map <- setNames(valencia_names$Valencia, valencia_names$Metaphlan)

metadata_CST_python <- reads_CST_python[, 1:2]  
species_counts_CST_python <- reads_CST_python[, 3:ncol(reads_CST_python)]

names(species_counts_CST_python) <- ifelse(!is.na(name_map[names(species_counts_CST_python)]),
                                name_map[names(species_counts_CST_python)],
                                names(species_counts_CST_python))

duplicated_cols <- colnames(species_counts_CST_python)[duplicated(colnames(species_counts_CST_python))]

dup_names <- colnames(species_counts_CST_python)

# Identify duplicated column names and their positions
dup_positions <- lapply(
  unique(dup_names[duplicated(dup_names)]),
  function(n) which(dup_names == n)
)
names(dup_positions) <- unique(dup_names[duplicated(dup_names)])

for (n in names(dup_positions)) {
  idx <- dup_positions[[n]]
  species_counts_CST_python[[n]] <- rowSums(species_counts_CST_python[, idx, drop = FALSE])
}

species_counts_CST_python <- species_counts_CST_python[, !duplicated(colnames(species_counts_CST_python))]

reads_CST_python_clean <- cbind(metadata_CST_python, species_counts_CST_python)

write_csv(reads_CST_python_clean, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/Output/CST/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_CST_estimated_counts_summed.csv")

#run this in python 
#script is python3 /Users/marbal/R_work/Clinical_trial_CHG_FLZ/data/Valencia.py -r /Users/marbal/R_work/Clinical_trial_CHG_FLZ/data/CST_centroids_012920.csv -i /Users/marbal/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/Output/CST/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_CST_estimated_counts_summed.csv -o /Users/marbal/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/Output/CST/260211_CST_output
```

```{r}
#| label: cst-table
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

#CST table 
cst_summary <- merged_data_CST %>%
  filter(!is.na(group_cross), !is.na(subCST)) %>%
  count(group_cross, subCST) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = subCST, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(-group_cross))) %>%
  dplyr::select(Group = group_cross, Total, everything())

#chi-square test of independence
tab <- table(merged_data_CST$group_cross, merged_data_CST$subCST)
chisq_res <- chisq.test(tab)
pval <- chisq_res$p.value

#add p-value to the table 
cst_summary <- cst_summary %>%
  mutate(p_value = if_else(Group == first(Group),
                           as.character(round(pval, 4)),
                           NA_character_))

cst_summary %>%
 gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Distribution of CST Subtypes by Research Group**"),
    subtitle = "Chi-square test for group differences"
  )  %>%
  cols_label(
    p_value = "p-value"
  ) 

write.csv(cst_summary, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/Output/CST/251121_CSTsubset_table.csv", na = "")

#fisher exact test
#contingency table
tab <- table(merged_data_CST$group_cross,
             merged_data_CST$subCST)

#Fisher's exact test with Monte Carlo simulation
fisher_res <- fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)

pval <- fisher_res$p.value

#add p-value to summary table
cst_summary <- cst_summary %>%
  mutate(p_value = if_else(Group == first(Group),
                           as.character(round(pval, 4)),
                           NA_character_))

#table
cst_summary 

#one by one for groups
df <- merged_data_CST %>%
  filter(!is.na(group_cross), !is.na(subCST)) %>%
  droplevels()

groups <- unique(df$group_cross)

if(length(groups) < 2){
  stop("Need at least 2 groups for pairwise comparison.")
}

pairs <- combn(groups, 2, simplify = FALSE)

pairwise_results <- map_dfr(pairs, function(grp) {

  sub_df <- df %>%
    filter(group_cross %in% grp)

  tab_pair <- table(sub_df$group_cross,
                    sub_df$subCST)

  test <- fisher.test(tab_pair,
                      simulate.p.value = TRUE,
                      B = 10000)

  tibble(
    Group1 = grp[1],
    Group2 = grp[2],
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
})

#adjust for multiple testing
pairwise_results <- pairwise_results %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj_BH   = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  )

pairwise_results

#collapse the CST (no subdivision)
cst_summary <- merged_data_CST %>%
  filter(!is.na(group_cross), !is.na(CST)) %>%
  count(group_cross, CST) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = CST, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(-group_cross))) %>%
  dplyr::select(Group = group_cross, Total, everything())

tab <- table(merged_data_CST$group_cross, merged_data_CST$CST)
chisq_res <- chisq.test(tab)
pval <- chisq_res$p.value

#add p-value to the table 
cst_summary <- cst_summary %>%
  mutate(p_value = if_else(Group == first(Group),
                           as.character(round(pval, 4)),
                           NA_character_))

cst_summary



tab <- table(merged_data_CST$group_cross,
             merged_data_CST$CST)

#Fisher's exact test with Monte Carlo simulation
fisher_res <- fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)

pval <- fisher_res$p.value

#add p-value to summary table
cst_summary <- cst_summary %>%
  mutate(p_value = if_else(Group == first(Group),
                           as.character(round(pval, 4)),
                           NA_character_))

#table
cst_summary 

df <- merged_data_CST %>%
  filter(!is.na(group_cross), !is.na(CST)) %>%
  droplevels()

groups <- unique(df$group_cross)

if(length(groups) < 2){
  stop("Need at least 2 groups for pairwise comparison.")
}

pairs <- combn(groups, 2, simplify = FALSE)

pairwise_results <- map_dfr(pairs, function(grp) {

  sub_df <- df %>%
    filter(group_cross %in% grp)

  tab_pair <- table(sub_df$group_cross,
                    sub_df$CST)

  test <- fisher.test(tab_pair,
                      simulate.p.value = TRUE,
                      B = 10000)

  tibble(
    Group1 = grp[1],
    Group2 = grp[2],
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
})

#adjust for multiple testing
pairwise_results <- pairwise_results %>%
  mutate(
    p_adj_BH   = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  )

pairwise_results

#Rvvcpos and control 
df_sub <- merged_data_CST %>%
  filter(group_cross %in% c("RVVCpos", "Control"),
         !is.na(CST))

tab_sub <- table(df_sub$group_cross,
                 df_sub$CST)

fisher_res <- fisher.test(tab_sub,
                          simulate.p.value = TRUE,
                          B = 10000)

fisher_res$p.value


```

The distribution of CST types across cross sectional groups is not statistically significant. Interesting observations are still that RVVCpos has the highest proportion of IV, while RVVCneg and AS have no samples classified in the disbyotic category. In addition, RVVCpos also has the highest proportion of samples in class III (*L. iners* dominated). The classification of RVVCneg samples seems to resemble that of the classification in Control. The AS group has a large amount of classification class I (*L. crispatus*).

## Heatmap abundance data

Another way to visualize the relative abundance data is through heatmaps. Here the relative abundance data is normalized by either log2, log10 or CLR. On top of the heatmap clusters of samples with similar microbial composition emerge. On the left of the heatmap taxa cluster together if they have similar patterns in data. The group to which each sample belongs to is also visualized as a color coded bar above the heatmap.

```{r}
#| label: heatmap-abundance
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

###########
# HEATMAP #
###########

#log2 normalization relative abundance 
log2_data <- merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional

log2_data[, 17:70] <- log2(log2_data[, 17:70] + 1e-6)

#only abundance data 
heat_data <- as.matrix(log2_data[, 17:70])

#get rownames from svamp_ID
rownames(heat_data) <- log2_data[[2]]

heat_data_t <- t(heat_data)

#hierarchical clustering
row_hclust <- hclust(dist(heat_data_t), method = "ward.D2")   #taxa
col_hclust <- hclust(dist(t(heat_data_t)), method = "ward.D2") #samples

#hclust objects to dendrograms
row_dend <- as.dendrogram(row_hclust)
col_dend <- as.dendrogram(col_hclust)

#clusters (adjust for how many color groups)
k_row <- 4
k_col <- 3

#colors for each cluster
row_colors <- brewer.pal(k_row, "Pastel1")
col_colors <- brewer.pal(k_col, "Pastel2")

#colors for dendrites
row_dend_colored <- color_branches(row_dend, k = k_row, col = row_colors)
col_dend_colored <- color_branches(col_dend, k = k_col, col = col_colors)

#taxa names adjusted and in italics
pretty_taxa_names <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("s__", "", x)
  x <- gsub("_", " ", x)
  x <- sub("^([A-Z])[a-z]+ ", "\\1. ", x)   
  x
}

rownames(heat_data_t) <- pretty_taxa_names(rownames(heat_data_t))

#extract group column 
sample_groups <- log2_data$group_cross
names(sample_groups) <- colnames(heat_data_t)

#color for each group
group_levels <- unique(sample_groups)
group_colors <- c("#F76C6C","#9B59B6", "#FDBF57", "#56B4E9")
names(group_colors) <- group_levels

#bar above heatmap
col_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Group = sample_groups,
  col = list(Group = group_colors),
  annotation_legend_param = list(title = "Sample Group")
)

#heatmap
Heatmap(
  heat_data_t,
  name = "log2(Abundance)",
  col = colorRamp2(
    c(min(heat_data_t), 0, max(heat_data_t)),
    c("#CC358A", "white", "#FF8C42") 
  ),
  cluster_rows = row_dend_colored,    
  cluster_columns = col_dend_colored,  
  show_row_dend = TRUE,
  show_column_dend = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8, fontface = "italic"),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "bold")),
  show_heatmap_legend = TRUE, 
  top_annotation = col_ha
)

```

The relative abundance data does not seem to lead to clusters of specific cross sectional groups. The clusters in samples are a mix match of different groups, the microbiome does not seem to drive the cross sectional grouping. The taxa creates a cluster of the three most abundant species and then a single cluster for the fourth most abundant species. *C. albicans* is in a relatively small cluster together with some other species that also have a little higher abundance.

## Candida appearance

Since the focus of the svamp project is *C. albicans,* identifying how shotgun sequencing picked up/detected the species in each sample is an interesting addition to the overall relative abundance plots. The mycobiome consists of approximately 2% of the total microbiome and thus the candida presence can seem to dissapear or not be as clear in figures of the total microbiome. Comparisons of total candida per cross sectional group is done with the Mann Whitney U test in the violin plot.

```{r}
#| label: candida-appearance
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

###########
# CANDIDA #
###########

mpa4_samplerows_groups_long_cross <- merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("s__"),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "Abundance"
  )

mpa4_samplerows_groups_candida_cross <- mpa4_samplerows_groups_long_cross %>%
  filter(Species == "s__Candida_albicans")

candida_violin_cross <- ggplot(mpa4_samplerows_groups_candida_cross, aes(x = group_cross, y = Abundance, group = group_cross)) +
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, alpha = 0.6, color = "black", fill = NA) +
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.2, size = 3) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = "mean", 
    geom = "crossbar", 
    width = 0.8, 
    color = "#B2007F", 
    linewidth = 1.5
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
scale_x_discrete(
  limits = c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"),
  labels = c(
    expression(RVVC^"cul.pos"),
    expression(RVVC^"cul.neg"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.pos"),
    expression(CTRL^"cul.neg")
  )
) +
  theme (axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
         axis.title.y = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 20, angle = 90, margin = margin(r = 20)), 
         plot.title = element_blank(), 
         axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, hjust = 0.5),
         axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, size = 20, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5)) +
  ggtitle("Candida Abundance by Group (Violin Plot with Mean)") +
  labs(
    x = "Group",
    y = bquote(italic("C. albicans") ~ "abundance (%)")) + 
  stat_compare_means(label="p.signif",exact = FALSE, comparisons = list(c("RVVCpos","RVVCneg"),c("RVVCpos","Control"),c("RVVCpos","AS")), size = 6, bracket.size = 0.5, tip.length = 0.01)

plot(candida_violin_cross)

ggsave("~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/candida/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_candida_violin.png", plot = candida_violin_cross, width = 6, height = 6)

  group_by(group_cross) %>%
  summarise(Median_Abundance = median(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),  Max_Abundance = max(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min_Abundance = min(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE))

write_csv(median_candida_groups_cross, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/candida/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_candida_per_group.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: candida-statistics
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

kruskal.test(Abundance ~ group_cross, data = mpa4_samplerows_groups_candida_cross)

#post hoc 

dunnTest(Abundance ~ group_cross, data = mpa4_samplerows_groups_candida_cross, method = "bh")
```

In the RVVCpos group there are 6 women for which no candida is detected. In the AS group only 2 women have detected levels of candida. In the RVVCneg and Control group no candida is detected. Kruskal Wallis indicates that there are differences in candida appearance between groups p-value \< 0.05, this was followed up by a post-hoc test. This showed with the adjusted p-value how the Control and RVVCneg group are statistically different from the RVVCpos group in terms of candida presence. The rest of the comparisons are not significant after FDR.

# Clinical score comparison

Analysis is also performed on clinical score groups. All cross-sectional participants are here subdivided into their clinical score group (0 - 5) which was determined during gynecological examination.

## Clinical score correlation

Besides just only the distinction in cross sectional groups it is interesting to see how the clinical score (discharge, dryness, fissures, hyphae, redness) correlates with the specific factors included in the score but also the microbial findings.

```{r}

#spearman correlation specific clinical feature with the clinical score

cor_features_score <- map_dfr(

  row.names = FALSE

  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(variable, estimate), y = estimate, fill = p.value < 0.05)) +

#differences in correlations between groups 
clinical_score <- clinical_score %>%
    mutate(across(-c(1,2), as.numeric))

grouped_score <- clinical_score %>%
  group_split(group_cross)

group_names <- unique(clinical_score$group_cross)

correlations_by_group <- map2_dfr(
  grouped_score,
  group_names,
  ~ {
    data <- .x
    group_name <- .y

    #proceed if there’s variation in the clinical score
    if (length(unique(data[["Clinical score (0-5)"]])) < 2) {
      return(tibble(group = group_name, variable = NA_character_, estimate = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_))
    }

    results <- map_dfr(
      names(data)[-(1:2)],  
      ~ {
        x <- data[["Clinical score (0-5)"]]
        y <- data[[.x]]

        res <- suppressWarnings(tryCatch(cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman"), error = function(e) NULL))

        if (is.null(res)) {
          tibble(variable = .x, estimate = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_)
        } else {
          tibble(variable = .x, estimate = res$estimate, p.value = res$p.value)
        }
      }
    )

    results %>%
      mutate(group = group_name)
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::select(group, variable, estimate, p.value) %>%
  arrange(group, desc(abs(estimate)))

correlations_by_group %>%
gt()

write_csv(correlations_by_group, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/clinical score/251105_VMBcandida_luminal_
          group_correlations.csv")
```

## Clinical score PERMANOVA and PCoA

```{r}
#| label: clinical-permanova
#| echo: TRUE
#| message: FALSE
#| warning: FALSE
#| code-fold: true

###################################
# CLINICAL SCORE PERMANOVA + PCOA #
###################################

#ordination points
ordination_dysp_cross_cs <-vegan::metaMDS(as.data.frame(mpa4_samplerows_cross_sectional_filtered_renormalized[,1:54]), distance="bray", plot=FALSE,autotransform = FALSE)

points_dysp_cross_cs <-data.frame(ordination_dysp_cross_cs$points[,1:2])

points_dysp_cross_cs <- points_dysp_cross_cs %>% 
  mutate(sample_rowname = rownames(points_dysp_cross))

#match the ordination points to the clinical score information
clinical_score_cross <- clinical_score %>%
    filter(group_cross %in% c("RVVCpos", "RVVCneg", "AS", "Control"))

clinical_score_cross <- clinical_score_cross %>%
    left_join(merged_samplerows_metadata_cross_sectional %>% dplyr::select("sample_rowname", "svamp_ID"), by = "svamp_ID")

meta_dysp_cross_cs <- left_join(points_dysp_cross_cs, clinical_score_cross)

#turn the clinical score into a factor with levels (still named the grouping factor group_cross)
meta_dysp_cross_cs$group_cross <- factor(meta_dysp_cross_cs$`Clinical score (0-5)`, 
                                                        levels = c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5"))

#PCoA plot (a form of overlaying the PCoA made before with the clinical score)
pcoa_cross_cs <- meta_dysp_cross_cs %>%
  filter(!is.na(group_cross)) %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, color = group_cross)) +
  xlim(-2, 2) +
  ylim(-2, 2) +
  geom_point(size = 6, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = brighter_pastels) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = group_cross), 
               type = "t",        
               level = 0.95,      
               linetype = 1,      
               linewidth = 1) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggtitle("MDS Bray") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = number_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = number_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(color = "Clinical score") +  
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
    legend.title = element_text(size = 25, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 25, face = "bold"), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20), 
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20), 
    legend.position = "right"
  )


plot(pcoa_cross_cs)

ggsave(plot = pcoa_cross_cs, "~/R_work/Luminal_cross_sectional/output/clinical score/251121_VMBcandida_luminal_cross_sectional_pcoa_clinical_score.png", width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300)

#pcoa without elipses 
pcoa_cross_cs_noelips <- meta_dysp_cross_cs %>%
  filter(!is.na(group_cross)) %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, color = group_cross)) +
  xlim(-2, 2) +
  ylim(-2, 2) +
```
